subject: Run-scoped delegated identity through the service shell and Sprintctl owner
source_of_truth: Sprintctl owns token digests, live run bindings, expiry/revocation and transactional revalidation; Vuoro composes its released API and enforces shell scope. Parent grant revocation after child mint is not live-introspected; explicit child-owner revocation or owner TTL/lifecycle event is required.
backends: In-process HTTP service and trusted owner resolver callback
Disposable PostgreSQL16 owner source conformance when explicitly configured
initial_state: Existing static or gateway primary resolver
Owner-returned immutable run scope and binding or unsupported old owner pin

operations.name: resolve reserved bearer through owner digest API
invoke permitted same-run read through HTTP
invoke permitted session-note write and retry same idempotency key
operations.synchronization: One owner row is committed; exact retry replays without a second effect

operations.name: refuse different run, repository or hosted workspace/project
revoke through parent identity, then retry cached delegated read and write
operations.synchronization: Owner revalidates the cached context and refuses post-revoke operations

consistency.object: Request identity projection and dispatch before owner action

assumptions.isolation: Source fixtures and disposable owner database; no production endpoints or migrations
assumptions.clock: Credential expiry from verified authenticator; shell UTC bound supplements owner clock checks

invariants: Reserved credentials never fall back to primary authentication
Only token hash enters owner lookup and failures disclose neither token nor owner details
Exact parent binding and singleton repository survive identity projection
Hosted workspace/project boundary cannot be bypassed by global digest lookup
Closed operation allowlist and exact run are checked before handler
Owner revalidation remains required after authentication and after revocation
Gateway verified expiry bounds child mint; primary source pins remain unchanged
Same-key session-note retry creates exactly one owner row
A previously resolved cached identity cannot read or write after owner revocation
Upstream parent-grant revocation alone does not revoke a minted child credential; child-owner revocation, settlement, exact-creator retirement, or expiry is required
faults: Upstream parent grant revoked after mint without child-owner revoke
